justification: This is the article's last round, and it earns the pass on design/UX. Fresh judgement first: Lighthouse is 96/100/100/100 (real numbers from lighthouse.json), zero console errors, zero console warnings, zero broken links (report.json 'broken': []), mobileOverflowPx 0, and the only build failure is the accepted NEEDS_MARKUS placeholder. Three figures each carry real information (Figure 1 sequence bands with per-band RTT and accent color for encrypted flights; Figure 2 chunked-body byte accounting; Figure 3 layer-wrapping with byte counts from the specs), all drawn on <=372-unit viewBoxes, theme-correct in dark (verified on desktop-dark and mobile-dark), annotations under the drawing, nothing the captions mention is cut. Heading hierarchy is one H1, specific H2s, H3s only under the long TCP/TLS sections, no boilerplate headings. Four content-bearing callouts (In .NET, Common pitfall, two Notes including one on NAT that used to be an unbroken paragraph), five exercises of different forms with collapsed, unspoiled solutions, a labelled 3-column timing table that renders cleanly on a 358px phone column, and a 28-item dated Sources list that reads fine at every width. Against the best-ranking pages for 'what happens when you type a url' (MDN, the AWS blog, and github.com/alex/what-happens-when, all fetched live), none has runnable/verified code, RFC-level citations, measured timings, working exercises, or diagrams that carry actual protocol data the way Figures 1-3 do; on presentation this page is at least equal to MDN and better illustrated than any comparator. Round-3 specifically claimed every remaining clipped line was targeted, and that claim holds under scrutiny: (1) the round-3 MAJOR, a sentence about case-insensitive header names duplicated back to back in 'Where the response ends', now appears exactly once (confirmed in the article source and in desktop-light-part06 / mobile-dark-part09). (2) Every token round 3 named as specifically cut is now fully visible at 390px on its own line, confirmed by direct screenshot inspection: `OrdinalIgnoreCase` (hoisted to `const StringComparison ic = OrdinalIgnoreCase;`, mobile-dark-part06), the `Host: {host}\r\n` header literal (mobile-dark-part06/11), `AuthenticateAsClientAsync` (wrapped so the method name is alone on its line in both the id=secure and id=names programs, mobile-dark-part11/14), `tls.RemoteCertificate!.Subject` (mobile-dark-part14, not cut at '.Sub' as round 3 found), and both `IPStatus.TtlExpired` and `IPStatus.TimedOut` (each alone on its own line, mobile-dark-part19, not cut at 'Timed' as round 3 found). The IsFraming `||` that round 3 flagged as off-screen is now the first token on its own wrapped line and fully visible (mobile-dark-part07). The timing-table header string round 3 flagged as cut after 'tl' is now split into two short concatenated literals and fully visible (mobile-dark-part11). The `OperationCanceledException` round-3 flagged as breaking mid-identifier in inline code is now prose-wrapped with the bare type name in a short inline span that does not break (mobile-dark-part08). The heading round 3 asked to be retitled to name bands 2 and 4 now reads 'Bands 2 and 4: TCP and HTTP without TLS' (mobile-dark-part06). The NAT paragraph round 3 flagged as an unbroken wall of text is now its own 'Where addresses get rewritten' callout (mobile-dark-part18). I checked every desktop-light part (fold + 01-17), every mobile-dark part (fold + 01-26), desktop-dark (fold + 01-02) and mobile-light (fold + 01-02) directly with the Read tool; nothing new is broken and dark-theme rendering of all three diagrams and every callout is correct. Held below a higher score for two small, genuinely open items, both already on record and neither a regression: Exercises 3 and 4 are still stacked back to back with no separating content (round 3 marked this optional, unchanged, writer-owned but low stakes), and the phone hero still stacks Published/Updated/read-time to several lines before the first paragraph (open since round 1, shell-level, owned by the integrator, and the placeholder byline currently makes it taller than production will be). A few code lines still lose a pure-boilerplate tail under the phone fade (a closing `);`, a trailing `.LocalEndpoint;`, a `\r\n` continuation) with the operative identifier already visible earlier on the same line or the line above; WRITER_GUIDE section 7 explicitly allows this ('fine when the tail is boilerplate'), so these are not counted as defects.
